title: Patanjali, fallen into open hands
hookLine: a tiny serpent falls into a praying woman's palms, and Yoga takes Samkhya's map and walks it
carry: yoga stills the mind so the seer rests
tomorrow: Is a scattered mind a bad mind?

cards: This path told this story back in year one. A woman named Gonika stands in a river at dawn, palms cupped full of water to offer to the sun, praying.
Far above, the great serpent Adishesha, on whom Vishnu rests, asks to go down and teach. He drops into her open hands as a tiny snake, and becomes a child.
She names him for how he came: pata, fallen, into anjali, cupped hands. Patanjali. Pictures still show him with a sage's body and a serpent's coils, a hood of cobra heads above him.
Today he returns as the teacher of a whole school.

teach.h: THE SAME MAP: SEER AND SEEN.
teach.b: The root text of the Yoga darshana is the Yoga Sutra, credited by tradition to Patanjali. Read it right after the Samkhya Karika and the furniture looks familiar. The seer and the seen.
The three gunas. The seen existing for the seer's sake, for experience and for release. That's Samkhya's map, nearly line for line.
But the Sutra asks a practical question: how do you get the confusion to clear? Its second verse answers: yoga is the stilling of the movements of the mind.

teach.h: STILL THE MIND; THE SEER RESTS.
teach.b: And the next verse says what happens then: the seer rests in its own nature. That's yesterday's crystal, with the red flower moved away.
Then Yoga adds two things of its own. First, a whole program of practice: ethics, posture, breath, withdrawing the senses, concentration, meditation, absorption.

Second, Ishvara, a special purusha untouched by affliction and karma, and the Sutra offers devotion to Ishvara as one path to stillness. The Samkhya Karika says nothing of Ishvara, and the schools are allowed to differ.

It's also why many classes in some lineages, Iyengar's and Ashtanga among them, in India and far beyond it, still begin by chanting an invocation to Patanjali. Yoga isn't stretching with a philosophy attached.
It's Samkhya's map, walked, and the teacher gets thanked first.

how: Students of the Yoga darshana read Patanjali's Yoga Sutra with its classical commentary attributed to Vyasa; practitioners in a number of lineages take up its eight limbs, and classes in some lineages, such as Iyengar and Ashtanga, open with a chanted invocation to Patanjali.

a school that stills the mind so the seer can rest

games.q: you've studied Samkhya's whole map: seer, seen, gunas, the count. Patanjali asks the next question. what is it?
o: how many principles are there, really?
how do you get the confusion to clear?
games.why: the Yoga Sutra is practical: yoga is the stilling of the mind's movements, and then the seer rests in its own nature.

practice: Sit tall, and give the mind one thing to rest on: the feel of the breath at the nostrils.
Each time it moves, to a plan, a sound, a memory, notice and come back, not forcing anything still, just letting the movements settle the way water clears when no one stirs it.
If you pray, you can rest in Ishvara, or whatever you pray to, as the Sutra allows.

wordCard.voice: Yoga. As a darshana, the school of Patanjali's Yoga Sutra: Samkhya's map of seer and seen, walked through practice, with room for Ishvara.

orig.note: Sanskrit: in the Yoga Sutra, the stilling of the movements of the mind; also the name of the darshana.

carryVoice: Your line: yoga stills the mind so the seer rests. Patanjali fell into open hands. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Yoga Sutra 1.2–1.3 (yoga as stilling the mind's movements; the seer rests in its own nature)
